title: Redburn: His First Voyage
author: Herman Melville
description: Herman Melville’s half-autobiographical novel of a boy sailor’s first voyage, drawn from his own 1839 trip to Liverpool. The Liverpool chapters show docks, beggars and emigrant ships. His ship ties up at Prince’s Dock, north of the Pier Head.

title: The Slave Ship: A Human History
author: Marcus Rediker
description: Historian Marcus Rediker on the ships that carried enslaved Africans across the Atlantic, built from sailors’ and captives’ own accounts. Liverpool sent more slaving voyages than any other British port. The Town Hall’s frieze includes carved African heads.

title: Dead Wake
author: Erik Larson
description: Erik Larson on the Cunard liner Lusitania, torpedoed off Ireland in May 1915 with nearly 1,200 dead. She was bound from New York for Liverpool, her home port. Cunard ran its fleet from the Cunard Building on the Pier Head waterfront.

title: Twopence to Cross the Mersey
author: Helen Forrester
description: Helen Forrester’s memoir of a family gone bankrupt and dropped into the slums of 1930s Liverpool. She was kept home from school to mind her six siblings. The title is the ferry fare back to the Wirral. The boats land at Woodside terminal in Birkenhead.

title: An Awfully Big Adventure
author: Beryl Bainbridge
description: Novelist Beryl Bainbridge worked as a teenage stagehand at the Liverpool Playhouse and drew on it for this dark comic novel. A stagestruck girl joins a repertory company in the bomb-damaged city of 1950. The theatre still stands on Williamson Square.

title: Tune In: The Beatles: All These Years, Volume 1
author: Mark Lewisohn
description: Beatles historian Mark Lewisohn on the band up to the end of 1962, nearly all of it in Liverpool. It’s long. John Lennon met Paul McCartney at a church fête at St Peter’s in Woolton, a village suburb, on 6 July 1957.

title: The Mersey Sound
author: Adrian Henri, Roger McGough and Brian Patten
description: Penguin’s 1967 collection of three Liverpool poets: painter Adrian Henri, Roger McGough and Brian Patten. Funny, sad, plain-spoken poems about love, pubs and the city. Their patch was Hope Street, which runs between the city’s two cathedrals.

title: Red or Dead
author: David Peace
description: Novelist David Peace retells Bill Shankly’s fifteen years managing Liverpool FC from 1959, in a deliberately repetitive, chant-like style. It’s long, over 700 pages. Shankly’s bronze statue stands outside Anfield, the club’s stadium, by the Kop stand.

title: Liverpool: Wondrous Place
author: Paul Du Noyer
description: Music writer Paul Du Noyer, a Liverpudlian, tells the city’s music story from sea shanties and the Beatles to punk and the Cream nightclub. The Cavern Club on Mathew Street is a rebuild. The original cellar was filled in in 1973.

title: Hillsborough: The Truth
author: Phil Scraton
description: Criminologist Phil Scraton on the 1989 crush at Sheffield’s Hillsborough stadium, where 97 Liverpool fans died, and the police cover-up that followed. His work fed the 2012 inquiry. Crowds held a vigil at St George’s Hall, the civic hall, when it reported.
